Hi all — I've formalized in Lean 4 (against current Mathlib) the basic properties of the mechanical word of an irrational slope, and before turning it into a PR I'd like to check whether this is something Mathlib wants and how you'd prefer it scoped.

For a slope β, the (lower) mechanical word is m n = ⌊(n+1)·β⌋ - ⌊n·β⌋. What I currently have proved (no sorry; #print axioms ⊆ {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}):

  • two-valued: m n = 0 ∨ m n = 1;
  • telescoping partial sum: ∑ k ∈ range L, m (i+k) = ⌊(i+L)·β⌋ - ⌊i·β⌋, hence density (1/L)·∑_{k<L} m k → β;
  • aperiodicity: for irrational β, the word has no period;
  • balance (the main one): any two length-L factors have 1-counts differing by at most 1.

As far as I can tell Mathlib has Beatty's theorem (Mathlib.NumberTheory.Rayleigh) but nothing on mechanical/Sturmian words or the balance property — please point me at any WIP I've missed.

Two questions: (1) Is a Sturmian/mechanical-words development welcome, or out of scope / already planned? (2) If welcome, how would you like it scoped and placed — minimal (definition + the above, under Mathlib.Combinatorics.Word.*), or building toward the fuller theory (factor-complexity n+1, balanced ∧ aperiodic ↔ Sturmian)? I'd carry irrationality of the slope as a hypothesis.

Happy to share the Lean file. Thanks!
I started minimal with the engine lemma as a small PR, #41861, and the word-level theorems (two-valued, density, balanced, aperiodic) are ready to follow if the development is welcome.
Thanks, #41861 seems like a welcome contribution to me, with a few changes to cut down on the size of the LLM generated proofs.
Thanks, revised and pushed. This was my first review :) Much appreciated.

Thank you again for the review on this back in July — I really appreciate it.

I wanted to follow up— after your approval it's just been sitting there quietly (CI still green, nothing changed). Does it still needs the maintainer merge step to get into the queue. If you're still happy with it, would you mind sending it up? Thank you again :)

I'm not actually a maintainer, just a longtime contributor, sorry if I gave you an impression otherwise. I would recommend marking the conversation in the thread as resolved. But otherwise, the unfortunate reality these days is that there is not a lot of maintainer bandwidth and PRs often sit on the review #queueboard for long periods of time.
Thank you so much for letting me know. This was my first time and I am still navigating everything. Much appreciated.
